# Data Quality Assessment Report: RLFSP (synthetic)

*Generated by `meldq` v0.1 on seed 20260601. All data are synthetic; no real persons or organisations are represented.*

## 1. Scope and approach

The assessment covers 3,365 household survey submissions across three rounds (1,200 households), a training register of 2,470 entries, 16 partner-quarter reports and the donor-reported figure. Dimensions follow USAID ADS 201 (validity, integrity, precision, reliability, timeliness) with ISO/IEC 25012-style extensions (completeness, representativeness). See `docs/dq_plan.md`.

## 2. Headline results

- **14 of 14 seeded error types detected** (recall >= 50%).

- Mean recall on record-level error types: **97%**; enumerator fabrication detected (recall 50%).

- Types detected only partially (recall < 90%): Enumerator fabrication (50%); Beneficiary double-counting across partners (79%).

- Flags raised: 756 across 26 checks.

## 5. Field verification (back-checks)

A risk-based sample of 332 submissions (10% of unique household-rounds; 50% risk-ranked, 50% random) was re-interviewed in simulation. Enumerators with >=2 major discrepancies are escalated.

## 7. Impact of data quality on the headline result (FCS)

| scenario | hh_rounds | participants_change | comparison_change | did | did_bias_vs_truth | participant_change_bias |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. Truth (clean, complete panel) | 2400 | 5.22 | 1.17 | 4.05 | 0 | 0 |
| B. Raw data as delivered (no cleaning) | 2245 | 5.49 | 1.19 | 4.3 | 0.25 | 0.27 |
| C. Cleaned (flagged records removed, matched panel) | 1774 | 5.21 | 1.49 | 3.72 | -0.33 | -0.01 |
| D. Cleaned + attrition weights (IPW) | 1774 | 5.65 | 1.87 | 3.78 | -0.27 | 0.43 |


In this run, leaving errors uncorrected shifts participants' FCS change by +0.27 points and the difference-in-differences by +0.25 (truth: 4.05). Cleaning removes 26% of household-rounds relative to the complete truth panel, which costs precision: data quality problems bias estimates *and* shrink usable sample.

*A = ground truth. B = what a naive analyst would report. C/D = after cleaning and attrition weighting. `participants_change` is the baseline-to-endline FCS change among participants; `did` is the difference-in-differences vs comparison households.*


## 8. Limitations

- Synthetic errors are cleaner and more independent than real ones; recall here is an upper bound on real-world performance.
- Back-check noise is simulated from ground truth.
- Fuzzy matching thresholds were tuned on this dataset; re-tune on real registers.
- Dataset-level tests detect that a problem exists, not which records are affected.
